entry: Target VM p15-dev-2604 created by a VBoxManage script (create-p15-vm.ps1): 4 vCPU, 8 GB, 64 GB fixed VDI, EFI, NAT ssh 2222->22. First attempt via GUI wizard produced a 25 GB disk with LVM (11 GB root) and was discarded.
Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic; linux-generic/-image/-headers held; unattended-upgrades disabled; no HWE kernel package; root on plain ext4; 4 GB swap file present.
LSM list has no bpf (lockdown,capability,landlock,yama,apparmor,ima,evm); lockdown [none]; Secure Boot off; clocksource tsc; BTF present (7,067,009 B); timezone UTC.

clang 21.1.8, libbpf-dev 1.6.3, bpftool 7.7.0 built with its own libbpf 1.7 and an empty features line, pahole 1.31, bpftrace 0.25.0, Python 3.14.4. Two libbpf versions on one machine: vendor one pinned copy.

P1: all needed VFS, security_*, socket and io_uring functions present in BTF and ftrace; vfs_readv/vfs_writev hookable (no kprobe fallback needed); __sock_sendmsg absent (inlined) so fexit sock_sendmsg would miss callers; no .isra/.constprop clones; all 9 needed tracepoints present.
Live test: bpftrace fexit:vmlinux:vfs_read /retval > 0/ caught 769 reads, 795,645 bytes in 3 s. fexit attach + return value work on the target.

P2: tracing, raw_tracepoint, syscall, lsm program types; ringbuf, user_ringbuf, task_storage maps available; inode_storage NOT available (needs BPF-LSM). bpf_get_func_ret shows 0 program types: bpftool cannot probe tracing-only helpers; confirm with first real load.

P5 disk: direct 1 MiB seq write 63.7/105/92.3 MB/s; buffered 64 KiB + fdatasync per MiB 65.8/93.4/110 MB/s. Min ~64 MB/s => ~21 MB/s at 3x headroom => ~330k records/s at 64 B. Large variance under Hyper-V.

Rule broken: old 5.4 VM deleted before the new capture reproduced v3.7. v3.7 now comparable only through existing recordings (s1_mixed) + replay. Rule added: export a VM (VBoxManage export --ovf20, sha256) before deleting it.

Repo ranahunter10/fiery-dragon created (public, MIT + BPF dual). Empty root commit on main; governance merged as PR #1, but with a merge commit instead of squash. Next: repo settings to squash-only and a ruleset protecting main (maintainer applies in GitHub UI).
Phase-0 raw evidence (files 00-05) imported byte for byte into docs/evidence/phase0/ with SHA256SUMS; tarball sha256 334b1b2a...a6b223. This is now the evidence location for E-0001..E-0008.

Refines E-0007: in 03-p2-feature-probe.txt bpftool prints 'Could not determine which helpers are available' for tracing, struct_ops, ext and lsm program types, so absence of bpf_get_func_ret/bpf_d_path there says nothing about the kernel. Both remain to be shown by a real load (get_func_ret INF, d_path from fexit OPEN).

Maintainer decisions: (1) journals stay CSV in the repo; (2) vendor the latest libbpf 1.7.x tag, to match bpftool 7.7 which generates our skeletons (exact tag fixed in ADR-0002); (3) swap off only while measuring, recorded per run (ADR-0012); (4) Hyper-V stays on; a paired on/off experiment decides later (ADR-0012).

VM creation script committed as tools/vm/create-vm.ps1 (content identical to the file that built p15-dev-2604; original sha256 c8bbdb85...a55a91, only the final CRLF normalised to LF by .gitattributes) and runbook docs/runbooks/vm-setup.md with the 2026-10-21 lessons. Gap: the evidence-capture commands are not yet scripted.

Census probe (bench/census/census.bt) + summarizer: counts per record class with the design's own hooks, cumulative counters every 100 ms, log-budget verdict vs P5 (21.2 MB/s). Dry run in the dev container (tracepoints only, bpftrace 0.20.2): 30 prctl renames -> rename=30; exec=56 and rename_exec=56; 1000 loopback sends -> snd=1001.

task_rename fires on every exec (exec sets comm), so a naive rename count double-counts exec. Product rule: comm change at exec belongs in the EXEC record; RENAME records only for prctl/proc-comm/kthread renames. Found by the census dry run.

The cloud dev container (kernel 6.18.44, bpftrace 0.20.2) can attach BPF tracepoint programs (tracefs mountable, BTF present) but not fentry/fexit via bpftrace (available_filter_functions not readable). Usable for dry runs of tracepoint logic; VM stays authoritative.

VM smoke run: on Ubuntu 26.04, cat copies data with splice() through an internal pipe, not read()/write(): cat of a 100 MiB file plus seq|cat (588,895 B) gave do_splice = 210,892,990 B = 2 x (104,857,600 + 588,895), and only 0.8 MB of rd_reg. A read/write-only capture misses cat's data flow entirely; the do_splice hook is required, and an XFER record must name both ends (file->pipe, pipe->dest).
evidence: VM census smoke run 2026-10-25 (raw file to be committed as fixture)

entry: bpftrace 0.25 prints compiler warnings to stdout before the JSON stream (0.20 did not); delete() now returns a value and warns when discarded. Summarizer accepts non-JSON only before the start marker, counted and reported.

On kernel 7.0 the exec-rename classification failed: exec=68, rename_exec=2, rename=98 (=30 prctl + 68). On 6.18 (container) the same logic gave rename_exec=exec. Event order during exec on 7.0 under investigation (diagnostic sent).

Diagnostic on VM (kernel 7.0.0-38, bpftrace 0.25): for an exec of /bin/true, task_rename -> sched_process_exec -> syscalls:sys_exit_execve all fired, but syscalls:sys_enter_execve delivered nothing. On the dev container (kernel 6.18.44, bpftrace 0.20.2) all execve tracepoints fire (enter 25 / exit 26 / raw id=59 26). Cause (kernel vs bpftrace) OPEN. Census now brackets exec with raw_syscalls ids 59/322 instead. Product consequence: per-syscall tracepoints can go silent without error, so the self-test must cover every hook.

On kernel 7.0.0-38 with bpftrace 0.25, every syscalls:sys_enter_* tracepoint tested (execve, openat) delivers 0 events to BPF, while the same events appear in tracefs without BPF (sys_execve(filename: ... "/usr/bin/sudo" ...), now with user strings), and syscalls:sys_exit_* (26 execve, 240 openat) and raw_syscalls (26) deliver normally. Kernel-vs-bpftrace cause OPEN; deciding test is a plain libbpf tracepoint program in Phase 1. Consequence: a hook can attach without error and deliver nothing, so the load-time self-test is mandatory for every hook.

Census probe validated on the VM (kernel 7.0, bpftrace 0.25) with the raw_syscalls exec bracket: exec 68 / rename_exec 67, rename 31 (30 prctl + 1), splice exactly 210,892,990 B, dd 104,857,600 B written. 20 probes attached, output complete.

Census workload runner (bench/census/run.py) with six light workloads. Dry run in the dev container (8 s each, tracepoint-only probe): all ran and stopped cleanly; io-uring SKIPPED (no fio there); exec-storm rename_exec = exec = 5,611; file-churn ~118k ops of each kind in 8 s. 17 runner tests; 8/8 mutants killed.

First real census, light set, 60 s each, all ok, 0 lost (kernel 7.0, bpftrace 0.25, Hyper-V on). Emitted records/s mean/p99: idle 6/0, exec-storm 2,481/4,274, file-churn 38,320/79,951, super-producer 105,731/221,670 (max 353,461), xfer 261/2,236, io-uring 3,483/23,099. Only super-producer exceeds the 21.2 MB/s budget (28.4 MB/s p99 at assumed sizes).

Super-producer budget overrun comes from one class: OPEN = 99.91 % of emitted records (find opening directories; 221,434/s p99). At 64 B per open record p99 would be 14.2 MB/s (within). OPEN record size (path in every record vs once per file) and a directory-open kind decide the budget: inputs to ADR-0005/0006/0008.
io_uring file I/O bypasses vfs_read/vfs_write: fio steady state shows uring 2,454/s while rd_reg is 7/s. The io_uring hook is required.

cp on ext4: vfs_copy_file_range (60) falls back internally to do_splice_direct; with 60 sendfile calls, splice_direct = 120, each exactly 64 MiB. One copy fires two hooks, so the product needs the one-layer rule (outermost hook emits, nested splice suppressed).

exec-storm reached only 77 execs/s on the VM (dev container: 633/s with a lighter probe). Cause not separated (VirtualBox-on-Hyper-V process creation vs probe cost). Needs P12 untraced baseline and the Hyper-V on/off experiment before any exec rate is quoted.

Design gap: no record class for file metadata operations (unlink, rename, chmod/chown, link/symlink, mkdir/rmdir, truncate), which carry core attack steps (rename into /usr/bin, chmod +x then exec, deleting evidence). Census v1 also omits connect/accept/bind and the capability family. Census v2 and ADR-0010 must add a META family and these.

Census v2: META (unlink, rmdir, mkdir, rename, link, symlink, chmod, chown, truncate), NET intent (connect, connect_fail, accept, bind, listen) and capability (mmap_shared_w, mprotect_exec, memfd, ptrace, process_vm_writev, io_uring_setup, module_load) classes; hooks and signatures checked in Linux v7.0 source (vfs_mkdir returns struct dentry * in 7.0). Added known-ops self-check workload (census count >= userspace successes) and an attach pre-flight (BTF + ftrace + tracefs). Container dry run: with a probe lacking the hooks, all 20 classes reported MISSED and the run FAILED, as designed. 62 tests; 8/8 mutants killed.

Census v2 on the VM: all 20 new hooks deliver on kernel 7.0 (known-ops: census >= expected for every class, 12 exact). Pre-flight found all 27 functions in BTF+ftrace and 9 tracepoints. file-churn unlinks exact: 68,878 = 68,425 deletes + 449 cleanup + 4 background.

The probe set changes workload speed: with the v2 probe (+20 fexit hooks) syscall rates were 0.17x (super-producer) to 0.70x (xfer) of the v1 run 29 min earlier, and file-churn did 3.6x less work; selectivity was unchanged (exec 0.193/0.193, super-producer 0.067/0.067). Census rates are lower bounds; sizing must use untraced syscall rate x census selectivity. Which hook adds the per-syscall cost is OPEN: A/B bisection next.
exec-storm under v2: mmap_exec ~212/s vs 26 execs/s, about 8 executable library mappings per exec. Emitting code-mapping records would multiply exec-related volume ~8x (input for ADR-0010).

Corrects E-0033: interleaved A/B on fixed work (find /usr x3 serial, 2 rounds) took 2.57 s untraced, 3.28 s under the v1 probe and 2.89 s under v2: v2 is not slower than v1, and tracing costs ~10-35 % here. The 0.17x-0.70x rate drop between the two census runs is not explained by the v2 hooks. Remaining candidates: host drift (runs 29 min apart under Hyper-V) and a concurrency effect (super-producer runs 5 finds in parallel). Selectivity result and the sizing method (untraced rate x selectivity) stand.

Parallel A/B (5 concurrent find /usr, 3 interleaved rounds): untraced 1.59 s, v1 1.85 s (+17 %), v2 2.06 s (+30 %). Contention does not multiply probe cost; v2 costs modestly more than v1 under parallel load. With E-0035, neither the v2 hooks nor concurrency explains the 0.17-0.70x rate drop between census runs; host drift under Hyper-V is the remaining explanation (INF by elimination). Method consequence: absolute rates need interleaved, repeated runs; single census runs are reliable for selectivity and class mix only.

Fixed-work baseline tool (bench/baseline/): find serial/parallel, 2,000 execs, 10 s churn, 20 s fio; untraced vs probe, counterbalanced order, mean/sd/CV per config, slowdown, CV > 10 % flagged not quotable. Container dry run: churn CV 82 % between 2 rounds (the flag fires), disk SKIPPED without fio. 15 tests; mutation 6/6 after strengthening one test.

Hyper-V A-B-A fixed-work baselines (3 rounds each, untraced vs census v2 probe): 2,000 execs untraced took 37.8 s (on, A1), 6.9 s (off, B), 28.1 s (on, A2), i.e. 53 / 292 / 71 execs/s, CV <= 7.4 %. The Windows hypervisor makes process creation 4-5.5x slower; disk 73 / 154 / 119 MB/s. Explains E-0029. Exec tracing slowdown +1 % / +11 % / +8 % (quotable).

Baseline tool defect: jobs contaminated each other through the page cache (untraced find-parallel 0.25-0.27 s in round 1 vs 0.72-0.99 s after churn; find-serial 17.6 s in round 1 after a fresh boot). find/churn means and their slowdowns from A1/B/A2 are not quotable. Fixed: untimed warm-up of each job, same configuration, right before the timed run.

Drift with no configuration change: A1 and A2 (both Hyper-V on) differ by -26 % on exec and +63 % on disk (A1 VM up for hours, A2 fresh boot). On this laptop relative measurements (overhead %, selectivity) are reliable; absolute rates are not. Sizing must use same-session untraced rates; ADR-0012 must fix the authoritative host state.

Windows 11: bcdedit hypervisorlaunchtype off is not enough while Memory integrity (HVCI) is on; VBS status stays 2 and HypervisorPresent stays True. Both must be turned off, and both restored afterwards (verified True / 2 / Enabled 1 / Auto). Runbook section 6a.

Maintainer decision: measurements are taken with the laptop in its everyday safe state (Hyper-V on, Memory integrity on). Only relative results are quoted from it (overhead %, selectivity, loss, class mix, all interleaved within one session); absolute rates are not quoted from this host. Absolute numbers, if needed, come later from better hardware. Goes into ADR-0012.

Warm-up re-run (Hyper-V on, 3 rounds, census v2 probe): the warm-up fix works for its defect (after a fresh boot the cold find-serial, 13.82 s, landed in the untimed warm-up; timed 0.31 s). But all 10 rows have CV 11.8-28.7 %, so no mean is quotable. The noise is fast: back-to-back untraced exec runs took 7.80 s and 12.80 s, 13 s apart; churn 19,990-39,417 ops/s; disk 72.9-171.5 MB/s. Three rounds gated on CV cannot resolve effects of a few percent on this host.

Corrects E-0038: the A-B-A runs did not show that the hypervisor causes the slow exec. With Hyper-V on, as in A1/A2 (operator note), untraced exec took 10.1-12.8 s (warm-ups 7.8-11.7 s) against 37.8 s (A1) and 28.1 s (A2): same-state runs differ by up to 3.3x, close to the 4-5.5x on/off ratio E-0038 attributed to Hyper-V. Something else that changes between boots was not controlled. B (off, 6.9 s) is still the fastest run; E-0042 (relative numbers only) is unaffected.

Census v2 probe and find: traced slower in all 3 timed pairs of both find jobs (paired ratios 1.19-2.79) and in every warm-up pair not hit by the cold cache; magnitude not quotable (OPEN). Likely mechanism (INF on 7.0): the census attaches raw_syscalls sys_enter/exit, so every syscall leaves the fast path (v3.5 on kernel 5.4: about 16 ns per syscall plus per-event cost). exec and churn: ratios on both sides of 1. disk: traced faster in 3 of 3 rounds (0.82-0.85), p = 0.25 by sign test, not interpreted. The census probe is not the product probe; product overhead is measured on the Phase-1 probe.

Maintainer decision: the overhead protocol changes to per-round paired ratios (traced and untraced back to back; median and range) plus an A/A control arm (a second untraced run each round) that measures the run's own noise floor, with at least 7 rounds; an effect is claimed only above that floor. CV stays as a drift indicator, not a quotability gate. Goes into ADR-0012.

Maintainer decision: census-probe overhead is no longer measured. It hooks every syscall through raw_syscalls, which the product does not (E-0045). The next overhead number comes from the Phase-1 probe.
Maintainer decision: install gcc-multilib on the VM, after a snapshot, so that P8's true 32-bit variant runs. It is dev-only and leaves the held kernel untouched.

P6 on 7.0: with a thread rewriting argv during execve, a tracer reading argv from the caller's memory at syscall entry (raw_syscalls id 59) matched what the kernel executed in 45 of 1,000 execs (4.5 %); the read of the new program's stack at sched_process_exec (mm->arg_start) matched 1,000 of 1,000. The no-race control matched 1,000 of 1,000 on both. Design input: the spine takes argv at sched_process_exec.

P8 on 7.0, int $0x80 from a 64-bit process: fexit vfs_read (2222 B) and vfs_write (3333 B), fexit security_file_open (both compat opens, with names) and sched_process_exec all fire for compat calls. raw_syscalls:sys_enter reports the i386 numbers (3, 4, 5, 6, 11) with TS_COMPAT (thread_info.status & 0x2) set, which are close/stat/fstat/lstat/munmap in the x86_64 table; no 59/322 for a compat execve. So any logic keyed on raw_syscalls ids must check TS_COMPAT. The 32-bit vDSO entry is still OPEN (build skipped: no gcc-multilib).

Two probe-harness defects found by the first VM run, both fixed with gates: (1) runuser not found, because subprocess searches the child's PATH (/usr/bin:/bin); fixed by an absolute path, and test_probelib really drops to nobody. (2) The P8 analyzer required TS_COMPAT = 1 but compat.bt prints status & 0x2 = 2, giving 9 false misses; the unchanged raw output re-analyzed with the fix gives 12 of 12. The VM output is now a test fixture. Synthetic fixtures had encoded the wrong assumption.

P8 with gcc-multilib (21 packages; kernel packages still held, uname 7.0.0-38): a static i386 program entering through the vDSO behaves like int $0x80. fexit vfs_read (1111 B, 2222 B), fexit vfs_write (3333 B), fexit security_file_open and sched_process_exec all fire with TS_COMPAT set. All 12 checks pass for both variants, exit 0. Every syscall of a 32-bit program enters with TS_COMPAT and its i386 number (17 distinct ids seen, none 59/322). Closes the open item in E-0050.

P11 on the VM (CPython 3.14.4, glibc 2.43, pip 26.2.2): the latest release of torch 2.14.1, torch-geometric 2.8.1, numpy 2.5.4, duckdb 2.0.0, hypothesis 6.170.9 and atheris 3.1.0 each has a wheel this interpreter can install, and pip resolves the whole closure with binaries only: 52 distributions from PyPI (19 of them GPU runtime: nvidia-*, cuda-*, triton), or 33 with no GPU runtime when the PyTorch CPU index is added (torch 2.14.1+cpu). Import-and-run on 3.14 and PyG's optional extensions are not checked.

Maintainer decision (blueprint Q-D3): the analysis tier runs on the VM's own Python 3.14 in a project venv, with torch from the PyTorch CPU index; no separate 3.12 environment. Based on E-0053 (all packages and the closure resolve as binaries; 33 packages, no GPU runtime). Reopens if the first analysis code fails to import or run on 3.14.

Corrects the P7 and P9 rows in STATE.md (2026-10-25), which said covered by census. The blueprint defines P7 as 64-bit and 32-bit connect/accept per candidate hook, and P9 as io_uring with and without CQE_SKIP and SQPOLL. Only 64-bit connect/accept (E-0032) and io_uring_complete on fio's default path (E-0027) were measured, so both are partial: P7 is needed before Phase 3, P9 before Phase 4. Found by the Phase 0 audit.

E-0021 and E-0022 (sys_enter_* tracepoints silent to BPF on 7.0) are graded MEAS, but their raw output was pasted in chat and never committed under docs/evidence/. The finding stands at reduced confidence (75 % in the audit); it must be re-captured by a script under tools/vm/ before any ADR cites it. Found by the Phase 0 audit.

The VM has no hardware performance counters: perf stat -e instructions,cycles reports no supported events (VirtualBox guest on Hyper-V). Cycle/instruction counting (Tetragon's perf-stat harness) is unavailable here. kernel.bpf_stats_enabled is 0 by default; enabling it and its cost are OPEN until the first Phase-1 program. Raw output transcribed from chat.

Maintainer accepted all eight proposed Phase-1 ADRs ("accept all"): 0001 platform, 0002 toolchain (incl. C for the daemon, Q-D2), 0003 hook policy (incl. revising D2, Q-A2), 0006 transport, 0007 WAL, 0008 schema (TOML, CLOCK_BOOTTIME), 0009 process identity (kernel-native key instead of task_key), 0012 quantification protocol. Merged as PRs #16-#23; CI skeleton (#15) and Phase 0 audit (#14) merged the same day.

The 7.0.0-38 vmlinux.h (bpftool BTF dump) has anonymous tagged members, e.g. "struct aes_enckey;" inside struct aes_key (5 sites). clang 18 with -Wall -Werror rejects them; -fms-extensions -Wno-microsoft-anon-tag builds them, matching how the kernel itself is compiled (INF). Added to BPF_CFLAGS. Whether the VM's clang 21 needs it too: INF yes, VM build pending.

Build scaffolding works from clean in the dev container (kernel 6.18, clang 18): static libbpf v1.7.0 and bpftool v7.7.0 bootstrap from the submodules; a CO-RE program at tp_btf/sched_process_exec, loaded through its generated skeleton and attached, saw the test child's exec with its tgid and a non-zero group_leader->start_boottime (seen 1, reserve_failed 0). Not the target kernel; the VM run is the authoritative one.

First build on the VM (commit 3334b50, kernel 7.0.0-38, clang 21.1.8): libbpf v1.7.0 and the BPF objects (with -fms-extensions) built, but the bpftool v7.7.0 bootstrap failed: openssl/opensslv.h missing. bpftool 7.7 links libcrypto unconditionally (program signing, src/Makefile line 128), so libssl-dev is a build dependency; the dev container and CI runner had it by chance. Added a make deps check that names the missing package, libssl-dev in CI and in runbook section 5a.

On the target (7.0.0-38, clang 21.1.8, commit d9d5492, after apt install libssl-dev; kernel still held): make from clean exits 0 and both smoke tests pass. core_smoke, built with the vendored libbpf v1.7.0 and a bpftool v7.7.0 skeleton, attached tp_btf/sched_process_exec and saw the child's exec with its tgid and a non-zero group_leader->start_boottime (matched 1, seen 1, reserve_failed 0). The first own program to load and attach on the target: tp_btf via libbpf, CO-RE on the 7.0 BTF and the ring buffer all work there.

Schema generator (ADR-0008) and the four spine records (FORK 64 B, EXEC 64 B fixed + filename <= 256 + argv <= 1024, EXIT 40 B, RENAME 64 B; 32-byte header). schema/records.toml generates the C header (static asserts), numpy dtypes, RECORDS.md and a BTF probe; lock.json blocks a layout change without a version bump. In the dev container the three-way check (generator, BTF of the clang-built probe, numpy) agrees on all 5 structs; the header compiles with gcc and clang -target bpf. 29 tests; 14 of 14 mutations caught. The filename/argv caps are inferences, to revisit with data.

Spine programs (tp_btf sched_process_fork/exec/exit, task_rename) and the load-time self-test, in the dev container (kernel 6.18, clang 18): all four pass the verifier and attach first time; the self-test passes 21 of 21 checks, with exactly the expected records attributed to the test child and grandchild (EXEC argv 17/17 bytes from the kernel's copy, start_ns consistent, exit statuses 0 and 7) and reserve_failed 0. C unit tests on synthetic records: 12 of 12 mutations caught. Not the target kernel; VM run pending.

Spine on the target (VM, kernel 7.0.0-38, clang 21.1.8, commit b456050; python3-numpy 2.3.5 installed for make check): make from clean and make check exit 0 (layout check 0 disagreements with clang 21 BTF and numpy 2.3.5); all four tp_btf programs pass the 7.0 verifier and attach; the self-test passes 21 of 21 in both runs with the same 7 records as in the container; reserve_failed 0 and seen == emitted for every type. A 5 s dump after the self-test recorded 0 records and the counters show no other events, so the idle VM ran nothing; capture of processes the tool did not create is not yet observed on the target (OPEN).

Second spine run on the target (dump 6 while the shell ran /bin/true x3 and sh -c 'exit 3'): 25 records, 0 invalid. Every /bin/true gives FORK by the shell, RENAME bash->true, EXEC (argv '/bin/true' 10/10), EXIT 0, all with the FORK's start time; sh gives EXIT 768 (3<<8); systemd and kthreadd forks captured too. EXEC inode 526290 equals stat's; the device is in the kernel's encoding (8388610 = MKDEV(8,2)) where stat gives 2050, so the decoder must convert. A 4-thread process exited with the leader's EXIT at group_dead=0 and a later non-leader thread's at group_dead=1: the end of a process is the EXIT with group_dead=1, not the leader's EXIT. The maintainer approved merging #26 and #27 and #27's size.

Adds to E-0066 with that run's full output (spine-dump.txt, sha256 as printed on the VM): counters FORK 8, EXEC 5, EXIT 12, RENAME 7 seen and emitted, 0 lost; the output holds exactly 32 records (self-test 7 + dump 25, matching per type), so every event the programs saw reached the reader. The first dump record is an EXIT of a process (tgid 4352) with no FORK in the output, i.e. started before attach: the start-up snapshot (step 4) is needed to name such processes.

P15W v1.0 specified (docs/formats/p15w-v1.md) and the C writer built (daemon/wal.c): 32-byte prefix + key/value metadata header with CRC32C; 40-byte batch headers with ring, count, first_seq, payload CRC32C and header CRC; one writev per batch; rotation by size and age; fdatasync on an interval, at rotation and at close; directory fsync after creating a segment; torn-tail recovery that never truncates corruption or a torn header. Dev container: 12 test groups pass, also under ASan/UBSan and valgrind; CRC32C matches the check value and the RFC 3720 vectors; a cut at every byte offset of the last batch recovers exactly; 27 of 27 planted bugs caught (make mutate-wal). Spec refinements beyond ADR-0007 listed as decisions in STATE.

Research note on quoting numbers that hold across platforms and on design ideas backed by numbers (docs/research/2026-10-25-measurement-and-design-inputs.md; sources R-011..R-021). Key inputs: lead with dimensionless metrics (loss, overhead ratio, completeness, bytes/record); quote the knee against the same host's ring-buffer ceiling from the kernel's own bench (published: 13.2 M/s at 1 producer, 1.07 M/s at 52 on EPYC 9654); Hoefler-Belli rule 4 versus ADR-0012's paired-ratio median; the L7 workload set shared by Nitro, NoDrop and eAudit; NoDrop's super producer; Nitro's per-CPU staging, 24 B records and in-eBPF MAC. Nothing adopted; seven decisions for the maintainer.

Ring-space probe (bpf/test/rb_size, dev container 6.18): an EXEC-style record reserved at its maximum takes 1,344 B whatever its length; bpf_ringbuf_output from a per-CPU scratch and bpf_ringbuf_reserve_dynptr both pass the verifier with a run-time length and take exactly 88/264/1,064/1,088 B for argv of 20/200/1,000/4,000 bytes. The spine's EXEC wastes about 15x the space for a short command line. Added to make smoke so the VM repeats it.

Answers to the maintainer's questions of 2026-10-26 written as proposed ADRs: 0017 spine flood resilience (the I/O super producer was designed out by ADR-0006's separate spine ring; the residual gaps were spine sizing from averages, max-size EXEC reservations, fdatasync stalling the drain, drain starvation and unlocated loss); 0018 measurement protocol v2 (no reporting rule broken: raw costs with intervals beside the paired Hodges-Lehmann effect, Wilcoxon, 10 rounds, knee against the same-host ceiling, one workload set incl. PostgreSQL/Nginx/Redis as functional tests from Phase 1); 0019 engineering gates (typed boundaries, P15_MUST_CHECK + one fatal path, hardening, fuzzing, analyzers, STATS + canary).

On 7.0 the kernel skips our tp_btf spine programs for some events. Tracepoint BPF runs preemptible (SRCU-fast guard), and the per-CPU, per-program recursion guard then skips any other task hitting the same tracepoint on that CPU, counting it only in recursion_misses. p15d with a 200-exec burst on the VM: spine_exec 13-22, spine_exit 12-17, spine_rename 10-14 misses; fork and net 0; EXEC + misses = forks. Our books close anyway, because the loss is before our first counter. It also explains the end-to-end case 1 failure (173 of 200 EXEC) and the demo run's FORK-less PID 12224.

The first open-cost run on the VM (PR #67; 220,000 open+close per traced arm, about 400,000 opens/s) ended INVALID in 19 of 21 traced arms: exit 4, invariant broken, 10-23 OPEN records and a few more CLOSE records missing from the WAL with no reservation failed and no PATH_MISSING; the harness reported no timing. Cause, read in the vendored libbpf v1.7.0 (src/ringbuf.c, ringbuf_process_ring, lines 256-265): the consumer position is advanced before the sample callback and stored even when the callback fails, so a record the callback refuses is consumed. drain.c refused a record whenever no queue batch was free and assumed it stayed in the ring; each such moment dropped one record, bulk or spine, counted nowhere but in the broken invariant. The path needs a writer that falls behind; no earlier run produced one. Reproduced in the dev container, spine only, with a writer slowed by a test hook: 398 queue-full moments, 1,899 of 2,000 EXEC records, exit 4.

The drain makes room first (fixes E-0173). p15_drain_room says how many records are certain to fit in the ring's batch (free bytes over P15_RECORD_MAX_SIZE, now generated: 4,232), publishing a batch it cannot use and acquiring another; the drain reads at most that many with ring__consume_n, the spine before the bulk ring, and waits with epoll_wait on the ring buffer's epoll fd, since ring_buffer__poll reads on its own. What does not fit stays in the ring. A callback that still finds no room sets the run INVALID with that reason (a bug by construction). New test hook --test-writer-batch-ms; it_p15d.sh case 11: 576 queue-full moments, 2,000 of 2,000 EXEC, exit 0, invariant closed. Unit test of p15_drain_room; six mutants killed (49-54); make check and the ASan build pass. Not yet shown: the fix on the VM and with file identity. Open: one unexplained failed check in 14 container runs of it_p15d.sh, its line not captured (the sweep now prints every FAIL line of a failed baseline). A design question it raises: bulk batches can take every queue slot, leaving the spine to wait in its ring behind them.

Under contention the path fentry is skipped for one open in ten: 12 processes opening and closing one file 200,000 times each on 3 vCPUs gave 2,400,018 session entries, 2,156,161 path runs, and 243,857 opens (10.2 %) with an OPEN marked PATH_MISSING, equal to the program's recursion_misses; the session and close programs (kprobe.session, kprobe.multi) were skipped for none; nothing was lost to the ring. Mechanism, read in Linux v7.0: a fentry runs under rcu_read_lock_dont_migrate with a per-CPU, per-program recursion context and can be preempted holding it (kernel/bpf/trampoline.c L1146-1153); kprobe.multi runs with cant_sleep under bpf_prog_active (kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c L2548-2585); bpf_d_path is offered only to tracing programs on allowlisted functions (bpf_trace.c L931-958, L1742-1743). E-0175's 0 skips in 4.4 M opens were one thread. Not measured: p15d's own shorter program, a real workload, and the network fexit programs, which share the exposure.

(2) The session's entry only registers the open file, with object 0; the program that reads the facts fills the object in (the path program, or the session's return when the path program was skipped). This removes from the entry the facts and the object lookup that the path program repeats (E-0188). ADR-0015 rule 2's 'whichever program runs first creates the file-map entry' still holds; no ADR changes. A CLOSE whose open had no object computed (both programs failed, each counted) has obj 0; the graph gives such an open file a node of its own ('u:' key, rule obj-unknown) instead of a false merge on obj 0.
